## What's new in 1.8.0

- **Cameras have their own list.** The list now has two tabs, **Peers** and **Cameras**: cameras are no longer mixed in with the intercoms, and **Add camera** is in the *Cameras* tab.
- **See your cameras.** Select a camera in the *Cameras* list and press **Turn on camera** to watch its live picture; press **Turn off camera** (or ✕ on the picture) to stop. It works with or without a call, and the button is only there for cameras, not for intercoms. The picture has no sound: call the camera to hear it (and, for a Tapo, to talk).
  - **TP-Link Tapo:** the picture needs the camera's *camera account*: in the Tapo app, open the camera → settings → *Advanced settings* → *Camera account*, create one, then enter it under **To see the picture** (⋮ → *Edit camera*). Tap **SD/HD** on the picture to switch between the small stream (default, less data) and full resolution.
  - **Zoom** with the zoom in / zoom out buttons on the picture (up to 8×), by pinching with two fingers, or by **double-tapping** a spot (2× there; double-tap again to zoom back out). Drag to look around while zoomed in. Works for every camera.
  - **Pan & tilt (Tapo only):** press the ✥ *Pan & tilt* button on the picture to show the arrows; tap an arrow to turn the camera a step, hold it to keep turning. It uses the same camera account as the picture.
  - The picture comes over the network as it's filmed (RTSP over TCP). If the camera can't be reached, the app says why and tries again every few seconds.
- **Other cameras (RTSP).** *Add camera → Other (RTSP)* now works for most other IP cameras: enter the camera's RTSP address (from its manual or app, for example `rtsp://192.168.1.20:554/stream1`) and its user name and password if it needs them. You see its picture, and calling it lets you **listen** if its sound is G.711 (the common kind for IP cameras). You can't talk to these cameras, so calling *Everyone* leaves them out. **Test** says whether it works and whether its sound can be played.
- **Zoom in on video calls too:** each intercom's video tile during a call has zoom in / zoom out buttons, pinch to zoom, double-tap to zoom in on a spot (again to zoom back out), and drag to look around; up to 3×, because call video is about 640×480.
- The Pi node keeps cameras (also RTSP ones) for calls, but has no screen for pictures.

Upgrading: install over 1.7.0 (Android: same as before) and your cameras, peers and settings are kept. Works with 1.2.0 – 1.7.0 intercoms; groups need 1.6.0 or newer on every member. Versions before 1.2.0 (including 1.1.1) can't connect, because they don't encrypt. The app is about 10 MB bigger, for the video player.
